TOP NEWS " In a rare move, Gov. Greg Abbott defends Medicaid funding for Texas" via Terri Langford - Texas Gov. Greg Abbott is doubling down on the state's fight to recover nearly $10 billion in Medicaid funding that the Trump administration is withholding from Texas hospitals. "Texas is working with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to protect funding that helps hospitals serve Medicaid patients and keeps critical emergency care available," Andrew Mahaleris , Abbott's spokesman, said in a statement. The statement comes two days after The Texas Tribune reported that the governor's office had stepped into a nearly year-long impasse between the Texas Health and Human Services Commission and Washington over the funding. The money helps hospitals close the gap between their Medicaid reimbursements and the actual costs they incur for treating low-income Texans. () " New polling on data centers shows how the issue could impact the midterms in Texas" via Fink - With the midterm elections approaching, new polling data shows that data centers could play an important role in competitive elections this year. A poll released by the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin found that a majority of Texans oppose the construction of data centers in their communities. In a sample of 1,200 voters, 30% of respondents strongly or somewhat supported the construction of data centers in their community, while 57% strongly or somewhat opposed. The poll also found that respondents are worried about the potential impact of data centers on their water supply, energy bills, environment and quality of life. However, they did feel data centers could have a positive impact on the economy locally, statewide and nationally. Jim Henson spoke with Jack Fink for "Eye On Politics" this week about the results and what they could mean for November. Jack Fink and Jim Henson discussed the issue of data centers, with Henson noting that the issue has become a lightning rod for discontent about the data centers themselves and their impacts on communities, as well as discontent around AI and anti-corporate feelings. Jack Fink also mentioned Gov. Abbott 's focus on data centers during a property tax relief rally in the Tyler area, which Fink believed was a sign that Republicans are feeling the issue from rural areas. () " Over 1.2 million Texans are on the voter "suspense list". Here's how to check your status." via - More than 1.2 million Texans, including 410,812 from North Texas counties, currently have a "suspensed"; voter status, according to the Texas Secretary of State's office. The good news? Being on the suspense list does not mean you lose your right to vote, but you will need to take a few quick steps to make sure your ballot counts. County voter registrars place voters on the suspense list when official county mail is returned as undeliverable. Common triggers include: Voters have until Oct. 5 to update their status. This is the deadline to register to vote. You can do this by visiting the Secretary of State's website. You'll need your current driver's license or ID card, Social Security number and the Voter Unique Identifier Number from your Voter Registration Card. () " Texas Governor Hits the Brakes on Flock Camera Funding" via - Gov. Greg Abbott has ordered all state agencies to pause funding for Flock cameras as scrutiny over the AI-powered surveillance devices has mounted. The order came as The Texas Tribune was preparing to publish an investigation detailing how a state agency has devoted at least $30 million to building up the state's Flock surveillance network by providing grants to local police departments. Abbott gave the order on Aug. 26, 2026, to halt state funding for Flock cameras, his spokesman confirmed. "To the extent that cities get any funding for those cameras, most of it comes from the federal government. To the extent any funding comes from Texas agencies, those agencies are clarifying that those funds cannot be used for Flock cameras," Andrew Mahaleris said in a statement shared first with the Tribune. () " Texas hospitals expect to lose $27 million a day in Medicaid funding starting Tuesday" via Terri Langford - When the state's new fiscal year begins on Tuesday, Texas hospitals expect to lose $27 million a day in additional Medicaid funding. The shortfall is the result of a decision by the Trump administration to withhold approval from Texas for about $9.8 billion in the next year from three programs, the bulk of which affects the Comprehensive Hospital Increase Reimbursement Program (CHIRP). This program gives hospitals additional funding to cover the difference between Medicaid rate payments and the actual costs that hospitals incur to provide services to Medicaid patients. Essentially, hospitals, which often are paid less than what they can spend on Medicaid patients due to outdated payment rates set by the state, are losing out on their additional reimbursement for 2027. Local governmental entities collect taxes from hospitals -- about $4 billion a year, according to the Texas Hospital Association -- and under CHIRP, the federal government matches those funds so that Texas hospitals can then use them to cover the actual costs of providing Medicaid services. Hospitals say those CHIRP dollars are critical and if they lose that funding, they will likely have to cut services to patients. "It is impossible for a hospital to take a huge loss on a Medicaid side of their portfolio and not have that impact services across the board, regardless of what type of insurance a patient has," said Sara Gonz alez, a THA vice president of advocacy, public policy and political strategy. Four million low-income Texans are enrolled in Medicaid, most of them children. Dr. Esmaeil Porsa , president and CEO of Harris Health, said "The impacts would be catastrophic for Texas' safety-net healthcare system," Robert Fries , the chief financial officer for Children's Health in Dallas said in a statement that this type of funding is crucial for children's hospitals like Children's Medical Center. Gov. Greg Abbott sent a pointed letter Aug. 7 to U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in which he stated that there's nothing wrong with the way Texas hospitals' local taxes are collected. Anna Stelter , the THA's vice president of policy and Carrie Kroll , THA's senior vice president of advocacy and public policy, also commented on the issue. () " A Texas Banking Billionaire and His Children Are Locked in a Bitter Succession Drama" via Glickman - A family battle over a billionaire's fortune, from boats and a jet to Dallas Cowboys tickets, is rankling the board of a small regional bank in Texas. Texas banking veteran Gerald J. Ford is ensnarled in a legal fight with some of his adult children over a large stake in Hilltop Holdings, the $2.2 billion financial-services holding company he forged. Four of Gerald J. Ford's children--including son Jeremy Ford , who took over as chair from Gerald J. Ford in 2025--are suing to wrest away control of their father's more-than-26% stake in Hilltop, worth some $600 million. The battle is over the control of Gerald J. Ford's stake in Hilltop Holdings, which is a significant portion of the company, and the outcome is still uncertain. () " UT Arlington president stepping down to return to teaching" via Maven Navarro - University of Texas at Arlington PresidentJennifer Cowley announced Monday, Aug. 31, that she would step down from her role to teaching at the university. Cowley was the first woman to serve as president of the university, a role she has held since 2022. The change is effective immediately. "As I conclude my service as president, I do so with tremendous gratitude for what we have accomplished together, deep affection for this community, and great optimism for UTA's future. I will never lose sight of what a privilege it is to help shape the lives of our students," Cowley said in a statement. UTA Chancellor John Zerwas said that when he learned of Cowley's decision, he felt gratitude for her commitment to stay at the university. () 2026 " Talarico Is Out-Fundraising Paxton and Flooding the Airwaves in Texas Senate Race" via Maggie Severns and Elizabeth Findell - Senate candidateJames Talarico began August in Massachusetts, standing beside a swimming pool on tony Nantucket, where more than 100 curious islanders gathered in sunglasses and sports coats to see what the bright-eyed Democrat on a hot streak in Texas was all about. The event, held at the cedar-shingled home of a former Biden administration ambassador, came as James Talarico made a private East Coast swing that included August stops in Martha's Vineyard, another Massachusetts vacation spot, and New York City, according to invitations that priced tickets between $500 and $13,500. () " Talarico needs to cut Paxton's edge with rural Texans to win Senate race. Can he?" via Eleanor Dearman - In 2018, Texas' Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate sought to run a different type of campaign. For years, liberal candidates had focused on Texas' most populous areas -- cities where Democrats largely resided. It was just a matter of getting them to turn out, the theory went. But Beto O 'Rourke wanted to try something new. He would famously stump in all of Texas' 254 counties in his 2018 race against Sen. Ted Cruz , zigzagging to communities across Texas, small and large. He lost a close race. However, in some ways, the strategy worked. James Talarico , the party's nominee, needs votes from everywhere. He doesn't have to win rural Texas; that's practically impossible. But if he reduces Ken Paxton 's advantage in counties concerned about water and private school vouchers, irritated over energy and grocery costs and angry about data centers, he improves his odds. "We're determined not to make those [campaign] mistakes of the past," Talarico said recently, acknowledging Texas Democrats have sometimes neglected areas beyond the cities and suburbs. "It's why we're constantly showing up in rural communities, in our small towns. Why are we speaking" to the concerns of voters there. () " Dark money in Texas Senate race spurs Talarico complaint to FEC against Paxton" via Gabe Kaminsky - Earlier this year, a super PAC supporting Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton received four checks totaling over $1 million from an organization called Preserve Texas, Inc. Preserve Texas is not registered as a political committee and has not filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission that could reveal where the money came from. Instead, it is a Virginia-based nonprofit, incorporated by John Plishka , the treasurer for Paxton's Senate campaign, according to corporate documents filed in Virginia. The arrangement, part of the dramatic uptick in American politics of anonymous, big-dollar giving, has now drawn a complaint from the campaign of Paxton's Democratic opponent, James Talarico , which accused Paxton and his treasurer of violating federal campaign finance rules. () " Affordability crisis takes center stage in Texas races" via Joshua Fechter ,Paul Cobler , Dan Keemahill , Terri Langford and Kayla Guo - In a state once considered one of the most affordable places in the country, candidates have popped up at barbershops and in voters' homes vowing to tackle a new problem for Texas: its cost-of-living woes. "Affordability has become the defining issue of this cycle and the voters want candidates to speak on it," said Michael Adams , a professor and director of the Master of Public Affairs Graduate Program at Texas Southern University. From housing to groceries and gas, Texans' regular expenses have risen considerably in the past several years. As those costs have grown, Texans have increasingly said the higher cost of living is one of the biggest problems facing the state. In the state's marquee Senate race, Republican Ken Paxton has floated tax breaks for families to help pay for health care and housing costs, and more ideas. Among the proposals from state Rep. James Talarico , his Democratic foe from Austin: abolishing the gas tax to help Texans' transportation costs and expanding tax benefits for parents with kids. () " Gina Hinojosa focuses on kitchen table issues as polls show the Texas Governor's race within five percentage points" via Fink - Statewide polls show the top concern among Texans is inflation and higher prices, and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa said her campaign reflects that. "Everyone's done with the culture wars. Nobody has, really, the luxury to be focused on this. It's about kitchen table issues. That's what this campaign is about," she said. A new poll released last week by the Texas Politics Project at UT Austin shows Gina Hinojosa trailing three-term Republican incumbent Greg Abbott by five percentage points, 45-40 percent. 10% are undecided, while 38% of Independents said they're undecided. Two months ago, the same poll had Abbott leading Hinojosa by seven percentage points. In the Real Clear Politics average of polls between June 3 and August 24, Abbott leads by 4.7 percentage points, 48.6 percent to 43.9 percent. Last week, Abbott's campaign began advertising on TV, and the Governor maintains a sizable campaign war chest with about $67 million cash on hand as of June 30th. In an interview, Hinojosa was asked how she is going to keep this a tight race as the Governor starts spending on advertising. () " Former GOP Texas Supreme Court justices back Democrat for attorney general" via Eleanor Klibanoff - Two former Texas Supreme Court justices appointed by Republican governors are endorsing Democratic attorney general nominee Nathan Johnson over their party's pick, Mayes Middleton. The race to replace outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton as Texas' top lawyer is, like many races this cycle, running tighter than usual. While Republicans have held the seat since John Cornyn was elected in 1998, several polls have Nathan Johnson within five points of Middleton. Tom Phillips , who broke the Democrats' stranglehold on the high court with his appointment as chief justice in 1987, and Deborah Hankinson , an appointee of then-Gov. George W. Bush , say they support Nathan Johnson's nonpartisan approach to the agency. The attorney general's office, which defends state agencies and statutes against legal challenges, frequently intersects with the state's highest civil court, which has the final say on such cases. "For attorney general, I look at who will follow the law and who will operate the office efficiently," Phillips said. "That's been Nathan Johnson's emphasis, and Mayes Middleton's has been more about using the office as a political tool to advance certain agendas." () " Despite outrage, Tarrant County approves 30% reduction in voting sites for November" via Rachel Royster - Tarrant County will have 224 Election Day and 47 early voting polling locations for the November midterm election after numerous calls for more to be added to the original list. Last month, Elections Administrator Clint Ludwig presented a suggested list of polling locations that offered to use roughly half the number of sites that were used in the 2022 midterm election. The Commissioners Court entirely opposed the slash, saying it was far too drastic. In their marathon 10-hour meeting Tuesday, the commissioners voted along party lines to approve 29% fewer Election Day and 6% fewer early voting centers compared to the November 2022 lists. Democrat Commissioner Alisa Simmons requested several sites be added to the early voting list and almost 150 be added to Election Day. The amendment was turned down because many of the early voting sites were unavailable or gave the southern precincts more locations than the northern precincts had. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick targets schools over 2,000 books he says are 'vulgar'" via - Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick announced last month that he will try to remove what he deems inappropriate books from school libraries. His message was clear and simple at an Aug. 19 news conference. "We're coming for the books," Dan Patrick said. Dan Patrick said this latest effort comes after school districts were not following the law -- Senate Bill 13 -- which called for districts to create more transparency over what books are in their schools' catalogs. Dan Patrick said over 2,000 titles are subject to removal. If the districts choose not to remove the books, Dan Patrick said he will urge the Legislature to consider another law that, if passed, could mean some districts could be taken over by the Texas Education Agency (TEA). Among the 2,000 titles was "Let's Talk About It " by Erika Moen and Matthew Nolan , a sex education book created for teenagers. "So filthy, so dirty, so vulgar, so pornographic, and for the ladies here, I wouldn't even want to show you," Dan Patrick said. Bonnie Wallace of the religious values-based group Recover America provided a list of 14 school districts in Texas that have the book. Spectrum News was able to independently verify that at least 12 of the districts have the book, including in some of the state's major metro areas like Austin, San Antonio, El Paso, as well as McAllen, Killeen and Galveston. () " At least 14 Texas districts at risk of school takeovers next year" via Megan Menchaca - More than a dozen Texas public school districts are at risk of triggering a potential state takeover if they do not improve student academic performance before the next year's A-F accountability ratings, data shows. At least 14 districts had at least one campus with a fourth consecutive failing grade, according to the preliminary 2026 ratings. That includes the Clarksville, Cleveland, Coldspring-Oakhurst, Elgin, Judson, Kingsville, Manor, Nacogdoches, Poteet, Runge, San Angelo, San Antonio, Spring and Waco school districts. The majority of the at-risk districts are concentrated in the Austin, Houston or San Antonio metro areas, with an average enrollment of about 11,700 students. Nearly every school eligible to trigger future state action has a larger percentage of low-income students than the state average, as well as higher rates of Black and Hispanic students. () " Texas' divisive overhaul of high school social studies lessons set to conclude this week" via Edison - A rewrite of what Texas high schoolers learn in history, government and geography is expected to receive final approval this week. The Texas State Board of Education will decide, for example, whether public school students must learn how "biblical imagery and founding principles of equality and justice from the Declaration of Independence" connect to Martin Luther King Jr. 's "I Have a Dream" speech. The board members will debate a recommendation that students learn about early Islam through the lens of "the Prophet Mohammed's brutal military campaigns against Jewish and Christian tribes, the normalization of slavery, and the taking of female captives as harem slaves." Another proposal would ensure students graduate with the ability to describe arguments against "the modern welfare state that emerged from continued expansion of Great Society programs." The Great Society refers to President Lyndon B. Johnson 's 1960s policy agenda that sought to abolish poverty and inequality. () " Gov. Abbott announces $138B investment in Texas transportation" via Ashton Yeaman - The office of Gov. Greg Abbott announced a $138 billion investment in Texas transportation infrastructure, including projects in the Greater Houston region, according to an Aug. 27 news release from the Texas Department of Transportation. The Unified Transportation Program was approved during an August meeting of the Texas Transportation Commission. The program's funding is divided into two portions, $95 billion for transportation projects across the state, and $43 billion which is reserved for routine maintenance and development. The total of $138 billion is intended to be spent on projects and maintenance over the next 10 years, according to the news release. () " Gov. Abbott, White House launch cybersecurity project to secure Texas water" via - Gov. Greg Abbott , White House launch cybersecurity project to secure Texas water In a roundtable discussion today with cybersecurity experts, Gov. Greg Abbott announced Project Watershed 250, a joint effort between the U.S. Government, Texas Government and private sector partners to provide free cybersecurity services to local water utilities across Texas. The project will exclusively be in Texas for the next six months as a pilot program. No additional information is provided about the project's future plans or expected outcomes. () #TXLEGE " Lawmakers added $1 to Texans' car insurance policies. The money paid for thousands of Flock cameras." via Ayden Runnels - In 2023, the Texas Legislature unanimously passed a law raising auto insurance costs for Texans by $1 to combat rampant catalytic converter theft. Three years later, a little-known state agency has devoted at least $30 million of that fee toward supercharging the state's Flock surveillance network, placing cameras along highways and streets from El Paso to the Louisiana border, an analysis by The Texas Tribune found. The Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, led by a board mostly appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott , has turned the $1 fee hike into at least 3,200 Flock cameras. The agency has awarded no fewer than 95 grants to help law enforcement agencies purchase and maintain about 2,000 Flock cameras. Another $15.9 million is helping the Texas Department of Public Safety add almost 1,200 more. Miguel Rodriguez , chair of the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, said during an August 2023 meeting that he hoped to use proceeds from the fee increase to "cover the entire state" with cameras. Rodriguez, who is also the Laredo Police Chief, sees the cameras as a powerful law enforcement tool, particularly to combat criminal organizations. But on Friday evening, after multiple requests for comment from the Tribune about its findings, Abbott's office said the governor was pausing all state funding for local grants to be used for Flock cameras. "To the extent that cities get any funding for those cameras, most of it comes from the federal government. To the extent any funding comes from Texas agencies, those agencies are clarifying that those funds cannot be used for Flock cameras," Andrew Mahaleris , Abbott spokesperson, said in a statement shared first with the Tribune. () " Comptroller requests doubling Texas school voucher program to $2 billion" via Kyle McClenagan - Texas' chief financial officer requested that lawmakers double the amount of money available for the state's private school voucher program, resulting in a total of more than $2 billion. In the appropriations request for 2028-29 biennium, Texas Comptroller Don Huffines asked the Legislature to raise the program's base funding by $1 billion so more families can use taxpayer money to cover private school or home schooling costs. Officials from the comptroller's office noted Thursday that the request was based on the number of current participants and students on the waitlist, as required by state law. Huffines also wants for an additional $226 million to accommodate funding increases for families currently participating in the program, which launched this school year. The Texas State Teachers Association on Thursday criticized the budget request, saying taxpayers need more information on who has signed up to receive voucher funding before raising the program's price tag. Recent state data shows that 70% of families who joined or have pending invites to the program already attended a private school or home-school. () " 4 in 10 Texas homeowners pay no school taxes. State leaders want to go further." via Gonz alez Kelly - Nearly 40% of Texas homeowners paid nothing in school property taxes last year after a decade of incremental increases to homestead exemptions, according to a analysis presented Tuesday by state Sen. Paul Bettencourt , R-Houston. The finding foreshadows a key focus for lawmakers in the coming months, as Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick in March directed the Senate Local Government Committee , which Paul Bettencourt chairs, to assess the impact of the increased homestead exemptions with an eye toward raising them even further in the 2027 legislative session, which starts in January. Gov. Greg Abbott , meanwhile, has his own plan to eliminate homeowners' school taxes , leaving only businesses to foot that bill. The Legislature last year raised the homestead exemption -- the amount a homeowner can deduct from the taxable value of their residence -- to $140,000 for most homeowners and to $200,000 for those over age 65 or with disabilities. It was the fourth time lawmakers have raised the homestead exemption since 2015, when it was just $15,000 for standard homeowners and $25,000 for seniors. Paul Bettencourt's committee staff found that 39% of all homeowners did not pay any school property taxes following the latest hike to the homestead exemption, up from 28% in 2024. Among seniors and disabled Texans, 61% of homeowners paid no school taxes. These homeowners' school tax bills also have long been frozen at the amount they paid in the first year they qualified for either exemption. State Sen. Molly Cook said renters don't benefit from the higher homestead exemptions, and argued the state cannot always rely on hefty surpluses to fill in the gaps left by lost tax revenue. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Corpus Christi, still in need of long-term water sources, again rejects desalination plant" via Colleen DeGuzman - The Corpus Christi City Council voted 5-3 Tuesday night to reject, again, an almost billion-dollar water treatment plant after a decade of effort and its long-term water supply still in question. The proposed desalination plant was intended to provide a drought-proof source of drinking water, but opponents questioned its high cost and the environmental impact of its salty discharge on Corpus Christi Bay. The vote was being watched by Gov. Greg Abbott , who criticized the City Council after it rejected the plant one year ago, saying the state might have to "micromanage" the city to protect the region's water supply. Before Tuesday's vote, Abbott chief of staff Robert Black called the proposed desalination plant "a tremendous opportunity to finally get ahead of the curve and be proactive to solve their long-term water challenges." () " Austin spent $719K managing homeless encampments in 26 days" via Chaya Tong - Austin spent $719,361 on homeless encampment management between May 11 and June 5, averaging $1,577 per site visit across 456 site visits, city staff told council members Wednesday. Outreach teams visited some sites multiple times, and most of the costs came from staff salaries and contractor payments. That was one of the key takeaways from a presentation Austin's Homeless Strategies and Operations office gave the city council's public health committee Wednesday. In addition to an analysis of the city's homeless encampment management efforts, staff also highlighted progress on the new South Austin homeless navigation center, investments in staffing, an expected increase in emergency shelter units and a projected decrease in rapid rehousing stock. () " Dallas police to shut off 321 Flock cameras after Abbott pauses state funding" via ' Chase Rogers - Dallas police will deactivate almost half of the Flock license-plate cameras across the city this month after Gov. Greg Abbott ordered a pause in state agency funding for the technology, the department announced Tuesday. The AI-powered cameras will be turned off Sept. 15. The change affects 321 cameras, police said, while more than 300 will remain in operation. Department officials learned of the funding change during a meeting with state officials Tuesday, said spokesperson Allison Hudson. Dallas has 684 cameras across the city, according to an online " transparency portal " that Hudson said was recently updated with information about how the police are using the technology. () " Central Health could raise property taxes. Here's what it would cost" via Nicole Villalpando - Central Health, the Austin and Travis County hospital district, is considering up to an 8% increase in property taxes for its 2027 fiscal year. That increase represents a $44 annual increase in property taxes for a median home value of $372,638. The highest the tax rate could be is 13.5195 cents per $100 home value. The current rate is 11.8023 with an annual bill of $460 for a home with the median value. If an 8% increase is approved by the hospital district's board of managers on Sept. 9 and then by the Travis County commissioners on Sept. 15, Central Health's budget will hit the $1 billion mark for the first time. In the 2026 fiscal year, the budget was $875 million. Central Health is tasked with caring for people making less than 200% of the federal poverty level. That 200% is $31,920 for a single person and $66,000 for a family of four. Central Health mainly does this through its Medical Access Program, which is similar to an insurance program for people who do not qualify for or can't afford another kind of insurance. Each year, the hospital district has been offering more direct care through its specialty care clinics, which began in 2022; a medical respite center that opened in 2025 and its CommUnityCare federally qualified health centers, which grew out of the city and county clinics. () " Brownsville faces higher tax bills as SpaceX presence grows" via Berenice Garcia - Home values in Cameron County more than doubled over a six-year period, and property tax bills are going up along with it, according to research from the Texas Real Estate Research Center at Texas A&M University. SpaceX's arrival in 2014 has led to the area's rapid rise in wealth, which researchers suspect also contributed to the rise in property values. And with the expansion of SpaceX and other industries in the Brownsville area, researchers expect home values to go up even further. For longtime residents of Brownsville, the largest city in the county, rising property values could mean rising tax bills. And for some, that means being priced out of their homes, one local real estate agent warns. Bob Torres , a real estate broker in the Brownsville area for 42 years, said he's alarmed that clients have told him that they want to sell their homes because they can't afford to pay their property taxes anymore. "This is the whole big dilemma -- who is SpaceX benefiting dollar-wise and who is it affecting negatively dollar-wise?" Torres said. Alan Guard , the Brownsville city manager, said not all home values are rising. "Definitely some of the houses we have are more expensive," Guard said. Lynn D. Krebs , an economist with the Texas Real Estate Research Center at Texas A&M University, said the increase in property taxes could similarly be attributed to newer, more expensive homes built during that time. () " Lubbock City Council hosting public hearing, 1st vote on budget, tax rate" via - The Lubbock City Council will host public hearings on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to hear from the public on its proposed tax rate and budget for the upcoming year. The public hearings and the first vote on the two items will be at 6 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 1, at the Citizens Tower council chambers, . Before heading there, here's a quick overview of what you need to know about the proposed tax rate and budget. At a meeting on Aug. 11, the Lubbock City Council set the proposed maximum tax rate at 51.3421 cents per $100 property valuation, which is effectively a 9.83 percent increase in the tax rate, according to data provided by the city. () BUSINESS NEWS " SpaceX to fund up to $220M in Brownsville water projects in exchange for land" via Berenice Garcia - Brownsville could receive up to $220 million from SpaceX for water and wastewater projects after the city agreed to remove roughly 445 acres of land from its city limits. During a special meeting over the weekend that lasted six hours, Brownsville city commissioners unanimously voted to de-annex the land, which is located near the Port of Brownsville. In exchange, SpaceX agreed to give the city up to $220 million for water and wastewater projects. Sheila McCorkle , SpaceX's vice president for Starship legal and regulatory issues, told the commissioners during Saturday's meeting that the company sought deannexation because the city was not providing any services to the area. Those services, she said, could be brought online through the city of Starbase faster and more economically. John Cowen Jr. told the Tribune on Monday, "This investment will allow us to reduce or completely eliminate our reliance on the Rio Grande River," "So if the Rio Grande River goes dry for any reason, we are assured water sustainability for generations to come." () " Tesla launches steering-wheel-free Cybercabs in Austin" via AP - Elon Musk sent dozens of self-driving Cybercabs without steering wheels or brake pedals onto the streets of Austin on Thursday, betting that Americans will overcome their fears of rides with "no control" and hop inside. The rollout of the gold-colored Teslas, which give passengers no way to take control in an emergency, comes as the company prepares to launch the service in other cities. Tesla shares have suffered amid a slump in vehicle sales, but they rose more than 5% Thursday on hopes that the futuristic-looking taxis will catch on quickly. "No steering wheel, no pedals," Tesla teased on X before the launch. Elon Musk followed with a post showing a giant Cybercab floating above the Austin skyline and later wrote, "A Storm of Cybercabs." Tesla trails self-driving taxi leader Waymo in the number of cabs deployed and trips completed. To catch up, it must demonstrate that its camera-only system can safely navigate streets and avoid pedestrians. By contrast, Waymo and another rival, Amazon's Zoox, supplement cameras with radar and a laser-based technology called lidar. () " Tesla advances Austin chip facility as Musk's Texas Terafab takes shape" via Guzm an - "Elon Musk 's vision to build the world's largest chip manufacturing plant is moving ahead. Dubbed Terafab, the semiconductor project calls for a massive manufacturing plant in Grimes County, east of College Station, while Tesla is developing a related research operation at Gigafactory Texas outside Austin. Now, new state records offer fresh details about work on the Austin semiconductor facility and the timeline for the Terafab plant. Construction filings with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation detail $150,000 in planned work across several projects at Tesla's Austin campus, including work on its semiconductor facility. One project filing lists $50,000 in ground-up construction and an interior finish-out for what Tesla calls its "Austin semiconductor fab." Another project, dubbed "north campus manufacturing," similarly lists new construction work on Harold Green Road. On Robotic Avenue amid its sprawling Austin campus, Tesla describes new construction for Cortex 2.0, the name the company has given to its AI training supercluster. First announced in March, SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab project aims to make chips for artificial intelligence and space data centers. In July, the rural school districts where the massive facility will be built signed off on school tax breaks for the project. Gov. Greg Abbott also signed off on the incentive shortly after. Now, a new filing posted by the Texas comptroller offers more about Terafab's timeline and economic impact. () " Southwest Airlines picks Austin for one of its first-ever airport lounges" via Alex Driggars - Southwest Airlines will open its first-ever airport lounges next year -- and flyers at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport will be among the first to try one out. The Dallas-based airline will initially open four lounges in Austin, Baltimore, Honolulu and Nashville, Tenn. It plans to build at least seven more in coming years "across high-demand business and leisure markets," the company said Wednesday. Southwest is partnering with JPMorgan Chase to launch a new high-end, airline-branded credit card next year, and cardholders will be granted access to the new lounge network. "Southwest Airlines has built one of the most trusted brands in travel by delivering authentic Hospitality that Customers value. Our lounges will be a natural extension of that experience, offering Customers a place to relax and experience the Southwest brand in a new way," Tony Roach said in a statement. "The introduction of a lounge network represents a strategic investment in Rapid Rewards and deepens our 30-year partnership with Chase." () " State Agency Approves First 'Permian Basin Reliability Plan' Transmission Lines as Paxton Joins Opposition" via Mitchell - The Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) approved two high-voltage transmission lines proposed as part of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan last week, clearing the way for a project that's drawn fire from a coalition that now includes the state's chief legal officer. The PUC, the state agency responsible for economic regulation of the state's electric and water utilities, voted unanimously on Friday, August 28 to amend Dallas-based electric company Oncor's certificates of convenience and necessity -- a permit that authorizes a company to provide a public service -- for two of the five 765-kilovolt (kV) transmission lines that make up the drafted Permian Basin Reliability Plan network. Oncor's lines are the first of the five to gain approval. On the same day, Ken Paxton , this year's Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, called on state authorities to pause further action on the plan. "The Legislature must be afforded the time to review the Plan and its potential impacts so it can then enact additional legislation to provide whatever additional guidance it deems fit," Paxton wrote. () " Ferguson completes $1.6B acquisition of Texas valve distributor" via Josh Janney - Ferguson Enterprises announced Tuesday that it has completed its $1.6 billion acquisition of Houston-based FloWorks from private equity firm Wynnchurch Capital. The deal closed Monday after customary closing conditions were satisfied. FloWorks, which generated about $1 billion in revenue in 2025, is an industrial distributor and service provider of valves and flow control solutions. Ferguson previously said the acquisition is expected to create additional revenue opportunities and about $45 million in annual cost savings. "We are pleased to officially welcome the FloWorks team to Ferguson," Ferguson CEO Kevin Murphy said in a statement. "Together, we strengthen our ability to serve customers across the non-residential market by combining our national scale and distribution expertise with FloWorks' deep technical capabilities in valves, automation, rotating equipment and fluid handling." | Friend,
We did something different in Wisconsin, and people are sitting up and taking notice. With a smaller budget than our Pennsylvania Supreme Court race in 2025, we couldn't run a full field and TV campaign. Traditional organizers. Mailers. Ads on every screen.
That wasn't in the cards.
So instead of doing less of what everyone else does, we did something no one else was doing.
Our co-founder Joe Bachman was interviewed by Wisconsin Public Radio about the cutting-edge voter contact technology we deployed in the state and how it helped us punch way above our weight:

| Here's the core idea: every Democrat deserves an organizer in their pocket.
An actual, interactive tool built specifically to talk a voter through exactly what they needed to know. Where to vote, what ID to bring, how the process works. One that could speak to Chris Taylor's record and positions on the issues. One that could answer questions with accurate information, at any hour, at a massive scale: we used it to reach over 1 million voters.
We share the concerns about AI's energy demands, economic disruption, and impact on workers. That’s why we worked with our partners at Convos to keep our footprint minimal. And for what it's worth: this approach has a smaller environmental impact than a large mailer campaign.
AI is becoming a bigger part of political campaigns. As we read stories about deepfakes and misinformation, Defend Our Courts is proud to lead the way in using this technology responsibly and transparently to have real conversations with the voters we need to reach. This also isn't about replacing the field organizers and volunteers who are the backbone of our democracy. It's about giving them a force multiplier. Reaching voters they couldn't reach. Having conversations that would otherwise never happen.
Wisconsin showed it can work and we couldn't have done it without you.
Tens of thousands of Democrats across the country pitched in to fuel this work. You made a difference in a race that far too few people were paying attention to.
Court races are like that. Under the radar. Underestimated. Until suddenly they're not. 2026 will have more high-stakes judicial races, with the same type of stakes as Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. We want to continue bringing our winning formula to key races on a national scale. But we need your continued support to do it:
[If you believe in what we're building and what we proved is possible, please consider chipping in $25, $15, or whatever you can spare today to help us build for more court battles in 2026?](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001qcoiQzlJYDAZUxXXCCqeOOt3APVF0_I3Khn2-FypUF_IKjW1Tfm5qKWRPRQ6Bzd2InwaG6IK2RmJKDjE_WRRCxkD0YFcOw41VrIK-Cly9B_rZdsG9kTJi0LNWES1RyJxynmpQcBbJGIdVvb4BF19AVVk4h8DqEJ_9jrnQaXKpEbnydomx49vRWKv3YUc4HlcrC0S1ICuixvfpX-Jua0bG5VfaG9Ut3pb6S-6-d6X-Qp4g88qi7qtX0wYxnM2Ot9nIH8WB-ian7E=&c=lBDtytKRJmW20uohH7VIQLXKsBGwIeoDclw7lCZGmrKKi_i980hTIA==&ch=UGe1-En1hNqWrj9sYdyXyxA0bp8e9cjeuUrN1o547Yo7z4XcbBArJQ==)

## Armed Man Attacks Ohio Gov Candidate
Police on Sunday [arrested an armed man](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQBeCnMZ3RYLPGFC5uQ7e3TYkGe1ic-GcFo0X79hHJI6QbaaRz9J2P-3zHmGJ5_MdMjtc6FzqPRMy0z3WL1WMJMSATMqP_2qlgjrMCZSSMEuyMnuOL5h6b4FYiRboh1w3WWqNAm2ZzwSi7htAtw9IB4LiiGVDD0ocANzJjE92VByPYDmDo-ha01r7X1N1Gu_jBiB4oRK57-1lj4Y3W9K4v2ltfc5Pcxvw8hP4n1CTUdJ5n65fjclx_oabrFGrC_JbouRZ5wSTumYLMWOQvTaip2V14njGleJhB9PDIGNNPCf9xm5dT3wEAAP__haB5Zw) who attacked Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton at the Canfield Fair, injuring multiple people before state troopers stopped him. Patrick Havas, 38, pushed through the crowd at the Mahoning County Democratic Party tent, [knocking over fairgoers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OnTAQRp_GdL7yD9dA4SIN3aZNiYZhuHcSYyMzAe3bR2yRF9j6kz6dc359TB_AifPrJ2wUZS1TputIJEJ1Km8uCHnhBYRABPBPpQwbT864oM2gTT8BCp80tdAscSVy5BuKtuv7PjjjQ_OOs4UOntaGwbkZwaxAK3YU1h7DYpxtON5_ZjC9Naaz7cN477H1ZJ9DP2MXVGtoYSn18btwljet6bOcVB9YtibFt8h-KP9DuVG58bquR57x9rh35ca9JBbGQ7nxC5wSoXDJyo1QN1r0TvUoWWPJay1ZDn2b69ffmWoGKZUh6f8hNGyfGlBK1nRSFo2gK2Z4DsEPz6bGZb84JT5Cp1rz2oDTF6d8M-8Z3b8AAAD___X-kfo) including an elderly man as he charged toward Acton. He was found carrying two pistols, a Taser and brass knuckles, though no weapons were drawn. Acton, a Democrat facing Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in one of the year's biggest races, was not hurt. [Both candidates condemned the attack](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAMhp-GdEQO5AgUFNekm2uvjBxwJtwRGGWsiebtV-xK-wLbWJYsf7--_-9tuWHKqdz_4EGet7oUup6ZmOlc6p5qwBJTRCZkxvD_pIJHWhQoI8FJsAsGTi9aRuyi34gU6Y78MFlrjQJtut1Huym7GufiaFc3BKXXaQC9wTYZMg675BsPHNgBYBrGHrTWYdQ0_HJ2DZMRI1BMXM_-X02Fd9ryu77o7EM9uux35sdT6N9CzULN13X1oayhHYWaG1qoGVwbbWtW8t7eSz3lt5_E4y0xcC3yS5Viv_ORu9PHx5VyTk8ziRHuB6b8Gcw_7Ovl1UcAAAD__7InfoQ), as did Gov. Mike DeWine, who called political violence "always unacceptable."
## GOP Unveils Lineup for Midterm Convention
The Republican National Committee [unveiled its speaker lineup](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O2zAUhE9DdTRoUn8uVDhI1G2KpNhSoMmR9WKKFMi3Enz7QLlCug8YzADzfX5MH5YCxedPu2LgOU0RRwlgRp7SQsnZ6MlbhmW27pUR7UqTVrqV6iZVP1nHtGOqbeWHGdAwFYZr1_d9q5Vpq2WY4WrjbDu7xj9833Smm9G4Gsbg0TZ1RcO5p26qvyrVXeuLMsa42uDa3PqH61pRK3jilC9_EkVeMId32pEvLq1VGBbmrQhzF3oUejyO47KWeGZCj4jyqwg9bikQkzvxeVbjishCjzk6mbHDhiLnrxDkC--YGLJssC9kGaiwnFOWK3lGXiUCHFOKRboUd8SThR5tlve7fvy4ff4SZkyOvDDfv51mcZTfyFuVB78dFAKVthO1eq6Wwr8H_J_i90H_DQAA___pZpvP) for the party's first-ever midterm convention, a two-night event in Dallas starting Wednesday with President Trump delivering the opening keynote and then the closing speech Thursday night. Vice President Vance [gives the keynote speech on night two](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LESmzAQBNCvEZ08h1BAFCrS0DltSuYsDnOxkBjpjMd_n7Gr9Gm3eLO7v6_zFTlyuv_CnbyseU70qpFEqMx54xwwLbygEIpgeBRKuPNswPQaRg1uxiB80myxWfxKZKhryLeDc6430PXN5mlcDIDp3Yr9ai2As6sJgOhGawLeGvYfD0ZwLcDQ2gt0XRdsR-2P0d3C0CsLtLDkcvmTOclGa3znk8ol5L2JfhM5qup-KjMpM93z8cmVmY5CtepCkbCSMlOh43mLHDDphMI5YdQh7zuLEGlMKT9ToKof9E5ZSNeD8EGl6jUX_Z38jxByOil9FGWmpvjleHGMXPtBWbjvyPHbTv7z1NObvwEAAP__WQaPDg) alongside cabinet officials like Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., plus Donald Trump Jr. and roughly 100 GOP lawmakers. But [dozens of swing-district Republicans plan to skip](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S2yAURp8GdXgQsBgXFM4P3aZJkVJzDdfWjSXQwI01efuMtsgLbP3NnPnO-fU-vQMtVB4_YMXA9zoV3PuCzNimOlNNUDJlYARmSM-GBVaatNJOqotUfoLE9MLJwpDDHVGjGTCMZ--908q4YQ4JbiklnUflxoTWG4_2zTjrxmRyynmgcPDURflRqfNoT8oYk6zB8e3ib-nshFWYiWs7_a5UeMb78re-sJ1SXYclzMxbF-YqdBQ67vt-Wns5NqEjFvmnCx0PLaFj5Rmb0JFn7CgfdZP_BbuEhrJvCE8qDwksV8qMbZWplhcWplokdPmB6LI_aRM6QpPXq759_3rLwsSaKAvz7csRFPf-E9s2tJC3nZaFujsLqx4r0PJxnD_Z-xX0vwAAAP__anWXXw). A survey of more than 70 GOP candidates and lawmakers found at least 45 opting out, citing scheduling conflicts and their own election positioning.
## Trump Floats Renaming New Mexico
President Trump on Sunday [posted a map](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3CAUhZ8Gd1gY8F9BMVFEEWnSpEhpYbgzJjHghTvD7tuvPPsIWx4d6eh839_rcjV-9_H-2wRQeEtLhFp2QIS8pM0na6LzziAYRGP_Z4gm-IUzPlA2UzYtxqJ_wiJN49QNgINoQHXjNE0DZ2JoNiXYbJ1crRjHcbBuEn3Xc8nZ0It17iU0Xp17bGZTx9jYyZYJIawU0PXztNpxIJKB85hy-y_5iBvc9o_0hNzaFJpdbYhHIeJCuCZc11rbUOLZEa4h0kchXJ9YhOuEG2TCNeZHOOiRChYazEG_uOKdRqg0wLu3iWJ6JRMge2sI1ybTy4Wvv3J9I0In6x0RP3-c8qCWP5CPJit3VL_vvgwjkewejN9fJ_Gbbp-KfwYAAP__MrqOyQ) of New Mexico relabeled "New America," days after a debunked online hoax claimed he had signed an executive order renaming the state. The White House's official account reposted the image on X. Trump followed with an AI-generated video on Truth Social showing him slapping "America" onto the state's welcome sign, calling the new name "so much more prestigious and beautiful." New Mexico Democrats pushed back. Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham said [the state's "name isn't up for debate,"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb0QYHMADQxdv6drResHP4aVgIvwSq39fpb_Q-Ur36Jyvy3wByrTdPqFg4LXOGx57RmZsc01UI2wLLcAIzBC_G25QaNZKW6lGqfwMkemF8wDdElZEjabD0DvvvdXK2C4FXM_2inGNcRy8dfocXRxHpZUar-hM7Ci8_9SofK-U64eTMsbEwWB_Hv01OisGhQtxbad7pY0TrvmnvrCdYi1dDon5sQvzIfQk9MQJE-X83oSeUi34VhJ62hkY5QEck9CTVW5w3sv8vMMmb432BEXuGcouuT3LQ254SCjYKILQU9fC8jgoZ9qtE4O6FaA_SMf_7PYK-jcAAP__7VqCtQ) noting it predates the United States itself.

| | | | | | Peter,

**Today is the day!**

Polls are opening across New Hampshire, and the Republican Primary will determine who moves forward to November.

In a primary election, **every vote matters** , _especially when turnout is low,_ and some races can come down to just a handful of votes.

**Do not sit this one out and let someone else decide what is best for you, your family, and your wallet.**

Get to the polls today and vote for the candidates who will stand up for our Live Free or Die values!

Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire has put together a list of 54 liberty champions who have signed The Pledge and committed to fighting for you.
[**Click here to take a look at the full list and make sure you know who is on your ballot.**](https://us.list-manage.com/15CYTre88n3?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)

Start a group chat.

Text your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers.

**Remind them that today is Election Day and encourage them to make their voices heard.**

Share our [list of endorsed candidates](https://us.list-manage.com/rXoUuw3sJPd?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) so they can see who has committed to fighting for our values.

If we want the best options on the ballot in November, we have to make our voices heard today. That starts with showing up.

[Find your polling location and voting hours here](https://us.list-manage.com/tBmVDjLA9SL?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70).

LET’S WIN!

## Houston’s Regan Hutsell Wins Miss America
Houston dancer Regan Hutsell [won Miss America 2027](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGutCAQBeCnwQ6DAyoWFH9jt397SzPiuJCgGGDX3be_cbNvcOvJnJzv_NymG_rg9_t_3MiU1xqnnc4cqBRKk4uPXOKeN58zbpS8xRLfGdcJBHRcDFzoCW3xT5oUVouZxTI0FZmm11p3rYS2cmYdGrQtrmSbVTb9LFHbdphnsWiUClTlzRUnBqGbRoCQddvpVq56EKpTrR06pgQtvsRUF0eFXpjX8I5PSrWNWxWMK-XITP5jMDIYz_OsrUtxv64MxgvEYPxi-OefwYipeBuIwZjojjt3j5IpBH5h-VfLQUDPARSITqr6cEeVzHKcPgSfu54pcd_Qh0-N8tf5ngZ-AwAA__-GToWX) Sunday in West Palm Beach, Florida, becoming the first Miss Texas to claim the national title in more than 50 years. Hutsell is the fourth Texan to win and the competition’s 99th titleholder. The [former Radio City Rockette](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp_G7iYC_BNcUGyT7m67pTWBcZhdbCyYOMnbr3xf4daf9Omc8-dr_kJOvD1-40pO3kueN3rVRCJU5pifVfJWV64VVyrsUfKn4jIbZUZQEyg7oxc-aO6xDe6uwqRbcvpqrR2HzgxtdJ3XXutrjziFwYc-WAx2WkzQ2k8W-5bdeacmZbVWRnWXYbRDt9hJ9WM_-GlsekWBJZeLRBJ6Y13SJx9ULj6vbXJRZK9N96sxt8bcdsp7onNqzG3JZaUCBQNn8CwfKNn_O_Wg0EGYKtRn2QtX3h5QeeWEhYWpwp3kRbSBRIK_-Q4SUSBS2ilApAIv3uAsA99EICyJgN4-PSsfBNqo62hH1RYX9henxHW8Nr16rMjpG1x-Gvxw5n8AAAD__5Ihmtw) and trained ballet dancer performed a jazz routine and won preliminary talent and fitness awards. She will receive a $50,000 scholarship. Hutsell studies health sciences online at Liberty University and hopes to become a physical therapist. Her community service initiative, _Your Body Is Your Home_ , promotes self-worth and a [healthier body image](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DWY-MsQ0EBJtM9jfdEPXHDVgyNnI3zHD71fw9wmYllar09P58TV8YYkjrb9xplPeSp0QvjiRCZdryyZIT74EZdyphRsk34zJppR2oAVQ_4Szhoslg7cdv5YemprHp-r53ttW23kZqOkVmnl1jvr1VXeu09YN2rrOktWnqMH7u1KD6plFatQ_retsu_aCMM3YeXGUU-SC5PGQjoTfyEu98UXnMea_juIkcXLW_Kv2s9POgfET6VJV-ftDhZwKMNwNvBC9kKIQx3pCoXPlkkAzHWfgkOHAlTFJuwEWoQMIrrCghrYAJ6F_ygXPxVIDeczw5XASNVl2nja3L6I9XiDGw6yqj1h1D_OGU__V7jfpvAAAA___Pq5Mx), drawing on her recovery from an eating disorder.
## SFA Provost Flags Three-Year Degree Challenges
Gov. Greg Abbott [directed the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOrCAQhZ8GOw2iIBQUt7H7b3tLM8igJCgbmF133_7GfYW_-5L5Mufk_PtZfiCmeG5_4UBL75CXE6-akAjLsudnpXzWI9YKB5a4AuVPhbAILlTLTcv1AivFFy4jNN467k3foO0nrbWSg5DNbntl5DQ4DCYA6F5PLhjnPMqg_RQm2UR7v-OG677ngg-dVFoOQRs-qlGuRrGRo4-US0c7Er6hhvTJLyzdmo8m2Z3oUdnwh4mZifm6ru4rUYnueWKXy8bEfGcwMXN9801fp6W9ILYfhNI6WHdMudR2zSnhhq3H7b6Cc5mIibkp1j-umFKsamIj3w6I6VuCfjvey4r_AQAA__9O5IUh) to recommend three-year bachelor's degree pathways requiring roughly 90 credit hours instead of the customary 120. The proposal aims to reduce costs, accelerate graduation, and meet workforce needs. The board is expected to submit recommendations by Dec. 31, and lawmakers could consider legislation in 2027. Eligible fields have not yet been selected. Stephen F. Austin State University Provost Jordan Barkley [said some programs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGunTAQBNCvMZ2RMRjswkUaupc2JVrMAlYMvvLug3v_PiK_8JppRjoazZ-v6Qtiiuf2Gw70_F7zdOJNCZmxTHv-Js4nHZEIDiwxAOcPwTpppXupnFR2gsDxwqmDavGzWlxToW8Ga21vWm2q3bvQDtbgPA9msGHRg7E9tM40a9c1zdJV0T-ccso2jdKqrU1vTbtap7q-M8H1olO4RM6l5h0Z30Br-uQLSx3yUSW_M79ItL-EHoUe7_uu_3LBpxR6fGyhR-WeGIQeaQX5KvnKxDJ_c4onkgw7pITnhiTvyLvc8iVhnjMzyQApyVZ-EIqcIeyYciG54FYQH2krcJDQY1X88rpjSpH6QXRqOyCm_xP5p9deXv8LAAD__xgojw0) would be difficult to compress. Programs governed by specialized accreditation may require clinical experience, internships, or other training that cannot simply be removed, leaving SFA to determine which degrees could fit the shorter format.
## Study Flags Metals in Border Toys
A [UTEP-led study](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0E2unSAUB_DV4OwYRPHBgMFLE2ev0w4NwuFJA2LgeL23q29ut9AN_D9-v77WLxtTPL5_2oyGnqGsB94tIRHWdS9Xo3K0HFuzGWt0lsqr2bAKLmbgGrharaP4wHWynTcb93ro0AwfSqlZjkJ2u5l0cMFr9FJt42BHPW9j8OgG77x0auqiecdxzdUwcMHHXs5KjkFpPs2TdHpmE0cfqdSediR82hbSqzyw9q7kLpmd6Gxs_GRiYWK577u_CM8e_cXE8v4TED0Ty7uGiaXhSZg3rEwsVJ7RQUayqYHdygOhIUGKOVKDUK7DQzxgEFACuD0mX_Fo8GaAcgDtCJjgtK2A8_D7YkL-GJmQn0PFP7CV6rH2O-XUVePPO6YU2_zBJv6dbUz_9tP_uj-M-BsAAP__DXyagQ) found that 12% of 333 children’s toys purchased in El Paso and Ciudad Juárez had total metal concentrations above thresholds drawn from U.S. or Mexican safety standards. Researchers collected 109 toys in El Paso and 224 in Ciudad Juárez over 11 months and screened their surfaces using X-ray fluorescence. Seventy-eight percent contained at least one element of potential concern, while approximately one in eight contained three or more. Toys purchased in Ciudad Juárez were about three times more likely to exceed safety thresholds than those bought in El Paso. Nickel appeared in more than one-third of all samples, while lead was detected in 3%, primarily in inexpensive children’s jewelry. Arsenic and cadmium were found only in toys purchased in Ciudad Juárez.. Published in _Environmental Pollution_ , the research is the first binational screening of hazardous metals in toys sold along the U.S.-Mexico border. Peter,

So let me be quick, and let me be honest with you.

I am Captain Mike Bouchard. Bronze Star recipient. I served with the 101st

defeat ISIS. I came home last October and filed for Congress twelve days later.

I am running in Michigan for an open seat that both parties have decided will
help settle control of the House.

The Democrats' Own Poll — MI-10

MIKE BOUCHARD (R) 45%
Tied — 45 to 45
CHRISTINA HINES (D) 45%
In a district President Trump won by 6 points

The Cook Political Report moved us to Toss Up on the strength of it.

Hakeem Jeffries needs seats exactly like this one. If he gets them, he gets
the gavel, and everything the President is trying to do stops moving on the
first day of the new Congress.

I do not have a political machine. I do not have a donor network I inherited.
My grandfather worked the line at GM for 33 years and my father has spent his
career in law enforcement, and neither of them left me a list of people who
write five figure checks.

What I have is a record, and whatever help I can earn from people who read

If you can spare a few dollars, it goes to work immediately.

body:
Last week, Donald Trump said that the only reason anyone would be opposed to the construction of a data center in their community is if they wanted to "end up being backwards and poor."
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=84%2E42639%2E3Ms110)
Last week, Donald Trump said that the only reason anyone would be opposed to the construction of a data center in their community is if they wanted to "end up being backwards and poor."
It's disrespectful to so many people who have legitimate concerns.
Concerns over the prospect that some of the wealthiest and most powerful people in the world are rushing us into a future with the potential to transform everything for the primary purpose of accumulating more wealth and power for themselves.
Concerns about the way big tech corporations have historically shown little regard for the safety and mental well-being of our children, or how the technology will be used in schools or to replace teachers.
Concerns over whether good union jobs are a part of all this construction, or what benefits are given to the American people since it's the collective knowledge of people that feed these models.
Concerns over the role of AI in surveillance and the potential for automated decisions by artificial intelligence when it comes to hiring and firing.
This is an issue that has the potential to eventually impact all of us in almost every part of our lives. The idea that there is no legitimate reason to be concerned is disrespectful.
**[I recorded a short video on the topic — one I hope you'll give a watch and while you're there please subscribe to my YouTube channel.](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/393?t=2&akid=84%2E42639%2E3Ms110)**

Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

# Take Action in Your Local Schools
| |
---
|
---
Now that the back-to-school dust has settled, we wanted to bring you two important reminders about your rights and two ways you can take action in your local schools. **1 — GET INFORMED: CURRICULUM OPT-OUT** Did you know Texas law gives parents the right to opt their children out of public or charter school instruction that conflicts with their personal convictions or beliefs? Exercising this right is straightforward: parents simply need to provide the school with **advance written notice** requesting that their child be opted out of the applicable instruction. **What does this have to do with vaccines?** Several vaccine-related topics are included in the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS) for students in grades K–3, 6–8, and high school. If you do not want your child participating in instruction covering these vaccine-related topics, you can exercise your right to opt out. We’ve made it easy. **Just print and complete**[**TFVC’s curriculum opt-out form**](https://xdzgmz.clicks.mlsend.com/td/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEyMDEyNjAsXCJsXCI6MTk4MDQ0MjQ2MDExMjgyNzI3LFwiclwiOjE5ODA0NDI5MDQzODM5OTg5OH0iLCJzIjoiOGY5NDlkMTJjNDg5MmY0MCJ9)**and submit it to your child’s school.** **2 — GET INVOLVED: SCHOOL HEALTH ADVISORY COUNCILS** Every Texas school district is required to have a **School Health Advisory Council (SHAC)** , and at least 50% of its members must be parents of current students. SHACs provide an opportunity for parents and community members to have a voice in the **district’s coordinated school health program**. Their work can include health education, physical education, health services, nutrition, counseling, the school environment, staff wellness, and family and community involvement. SHACs are required to meet at least four times during the school year, making them an important avenue for parents who want to be informed, engaged, and involved in decisions affecting their children. **Interested in serving on your district’s SHAC?** Start by visiting your school district’s website. SHAC information is often listed under the “Health Services” department. From there, reach out to the SHAC Facilitator to ask about current vacancies and how to apply. **TFVC is committed to equipping you with the knowledge and resources you need to advocate for your family and advance medical liberty in your community.**

# [What's it like to serve in Congress?](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2841627&post_id=156896806&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTU2ODk2ODA2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODg4NzA3NzUsImV4cCI6MTc5MTQ2Mjc3NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI4NDE2MjciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.eeDiwHuvX3nmCWIrCv9SH6P-8fhum15wuGrvWwN_yF8)
### There are two kinds of Members in Congress, and they're not Democrats and Republicans.
| | [Congressman Wiley Nickel](https://substack.com/@wileynickel)
---
| Sep 8
---

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcc29166-6062-4bf7-bc3a-49eb4d781b03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
First thing to know: it's really hard to get to the US House of Representatives. Bill Clinton lost a House race in 1974, George W. Bush lost one in 1978 and so did Barack Obama in 2000. Three future presidents, all of them tried and failed to get to the House.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/510f9afc-db9c-45e8-a39f-74da61b41882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I made it in 2022, in one of the most competitive House races in the country, flipping one of just six Republican seats in the whole nation from red to blue. It was brutal. But here's the funny part: once you're in, the system practically bolts you to the chair. Your odds of getting re-elected? 97%.
The whole thing is built to protect incumbents, and it works like a charm. Poll after poll says the same thing: Americans hate Congress, but they love their own member of Congress.
So here's what to expect once you get there.
You get paid $174,000 a year, a number that hasn't budged since 2009. You also get an official budget of close to $2 million a year, and you can spend it pretty much however you want. Most of it goes to staff, the folks who answer the phones, track legislation, and help constituents untangle their problems with federal agencies. The rest covers your travel, your district office rent, communications, big dry-erase checks and the other costs of the job.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/510f9afc-db9c-45e8-a39f-74da61b41882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The message here is simple: you get to choose your own adventure. Spend your time and your budget how you see fit. And the best members are the ones who actually use all of it to make people's lives better.
In my two years, my office answered more than 70,000 questions from constituents and helped over 1,600 of them fix problems with federal agencies, clawing back nearly $2.8 million that was rightfully theirs. It's a great way to make a lot of friends. It's also, not coincidentally, how you end up on the right side of that 97% figure.
Most members are doing that work, and it's genuinely good. But it's not the whole story. The question I really want to answer is the bigger one: why isn't Congress working?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/510f9afc-db9c-45e8-a39f-74da61b41882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here's what nobody tells you until you get there. There are two kinds of members, and I'm not talking about Democrats and Republicans. I'm talking about the 90% who got elected in safe seats and the less than 10% who came from real battlegrounds.
If you're in a safe seat, you're basically guaranteed re-election as long as you win your primary. And almost nobody loses their primary. So the only thing you really have to worry about is your own party's base if you're part of that 90%. There's zero incentive to talk to the people in the middle or work across the aisle. That's a big part of why the last Congress was one of the least productive since 1860. You don't have to get anything done to keep your job. You just have to keep your base happy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/510f9afc-db9c-45e8-a39f-74da61b41882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now compare that to the battleground members, the ones in truly competitive districts like mine was. There's only about 40 of us left out of 435, and that number keeps shrinking. You can thank gerrymandering for that.
When your district could go either way, you're forced to do the thing Congress is supposed to do: listen to everybody, find the middle, get something done. And if you can pull that off, you're effective no matter who runs the House, the Senate, or the White House.
That's the whole game, really. Most members want to stay because the perks are great and you can do real good with the job. And thanks to safe seats and the incumbency advantage, staying is a whole lot easier than getting there was. Congress would work much better if more members had to earn it every two years instead of coasting, if they were rewarded for working across the aisle instead of getting into partisan food fights.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/510f9afc-db9c-45e8-a39f-74da61b41882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As for me, Republican gerrymandering in North Carolina erased my district and took my 97% down to 0% with one stroke of a pen. But I still believe in the US Congress, and in the members who show up and do the right thing every day. It comes down to paying attention. The more people understand what their member is actually up to, and push them to serve everyone they represent, the better our democracy works.
-- Wiley

P.S. That thing everybody says about members of Congress getting free health care and pensions for life? Not true. You're treated like any other federal employee and you pay into the retirement system out of every paycheck, same as everyone else. You have to serve five years for a pension, and then you only get a slice of your salary. For a member who serves five-years, that's about $8,700 a year. Not exactly a golden parachute.

If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

On January 3rd, 2021, I stood in the House chamber and swore to support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic.

Three days later, the Capitol was attacked, and I had a choice to make: _be a politician, or be a patriot._

**I put our republic first: I served on the January 6th Committee, seeking truth, justice, and accountability for the American people.**

That decision may have cost me my House seat in 2022, after an onslaught of MAGA cash targeted our district. But I’d make the same choice all over again, because I swore an oath—the same oath I swore at 17 when I entered the Naval Academy—to protect the country I love.

**That’s why I’m running for Congress in 2026.**

I’m running to help families get ahead instead of just getting by, to ensure veterans get the support they need, and to defend our Constitution.

These aren’t just talking points, Peter. **We _can win this_**. We’ve already done so twice before. And last November, Virginians proved they’re intent on a new direction.

I’m ready to bring tough leadership to communities across Hampton Roads, but I can’t go it alone. I’m counting on patriots like you to join me on the right side of history.

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: The antidote to Drag Queen Story Hour
body:
We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded
ALA.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e926140/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvTUNyUGt5TUpjNg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MDg/LbmNscExCU0V6YQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNaMU50d0U4Y1FLeDlsc10/gaqAMDQ/s2v09713b57

Patriot,

If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox
News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, PLEASE LET ME
TELL YOU WHY IT’S SO CRITICAL.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the
library with a kind but stern librarian.

She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny _and _The
Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam
by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_,
_Treasure Island _and _Charlotte’s Web_.

BUT TODAY, ALL THAT HAS CHANGED.

Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of
the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used
to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+
writers and voices.’

Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn _and _To Kill
a Mockingbird _“racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls
Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her
“problematic’ _Little House _series.

And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for
“Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to
children of all ages...

A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their
kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism,
environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else
that activists believe in and fight for.”

Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a
new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the
air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change
the world.”

Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a
prince who marries a knight instead of a princess.

And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A
“family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to
“work it.”

I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New
York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true.

[Image showing people, person, and baby]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour”

THAT’S WHY PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY ARE RISING UP
THROUGH SEE YOU AT THE LIBRARY DAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and
George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA.

AND AS A RESULT, A NEW GENERATION OF PINK-HAIRED, ACTIVIST LIBRARIANS
HAVE MADE IT THEIR MISSION TO FILL LIBRARY SHELVES WITH ANTI-AMERICAN,
LGBTQ-FRIENDLY, AND EXPLICITLY SEXUAL CONTENT.

Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library
celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type
of religion.

Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to
be a “parent-free” zone.

The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick _about a
cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa _filled with graphic nudity, and
_Darkstalker _featuring gory violence and domestic abuse.

BUT HERE’S WHAT’S REALLY ALARMING.

We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my
family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t
check out those inappropriate books.”

That may be good for your family -- for now.

BUT MEANWHILE, THE ALA USES OUR TAXPAYER-FUNDED LIBRARIES TO LURE IN
MILLIONS OF OTHER CHILDREN WHO GROW UP TO BE THE VERY ACTIVISTS WHO
ARE DESTROYING OUR COUNTRY AND CONSERVATIVE VALUES!

I HOPE YOU SEE WHY I NEED YOUR HELP TODAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

My name is Kirk Cameron.

Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing
Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof”
and “Left Behind.”

I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist
values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood.

But the gospel saved me.

I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a
husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian.

When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to
indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America
messages, I knew I had a duty to take action.

So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children
how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit.

THEN I DECIDED TO GO ONE STEP FURTHER AND COUNTER THOSE AWFUL “DRAG
QUEEN STORY HOURS” WITH CONSERVATIVE STORY HOURS FILLED WITH THE
CLASSIC BOOKS YOU AND I GREW UP WITH, PLUS NEW WHOLESOME BOOKS LIKE
MINE THAT CAPTIVATE CHILDREN WITH LESSONS IN BRAVERY, HONESTY,
KINDNESS, AND PATRIOTISM.

And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit.

* Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.

* The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out
including booking all the event rooms for themselves.

* Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi
(that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse
and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored
moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and
on.

I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so
vile.

In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them
that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States.

AND THOUSANDS OF PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS BROUGHT THEIR LITTLE ONES TO
THOSE “STORY HOURS” WHERE WE PLEDGED ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG, SANG
“GOD BLESS AMERICA”, AND READ WHOLESOME AND GODLY BOOKS.

It was incredible.

But here’s the greatest part...

From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could
host “Story Hours” of their own.

And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement
was born.

Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at
201 libraries in 46 states.

On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours”

filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God.

Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a
very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and
reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries.

AND THIS YEAR, HONORING AMERICA’S 250TH BIRTHDAY, MY AMBITIOUS GOAL
IS TO EXPAND “SEE YOU AT THE LIBRARY DAY” TO REACH 250,000
CHILDREN.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you!

The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host
“Story Hours” has been overwhelming.

That’s a very good thing.

But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these
volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for
250,000 children.

THAT’S WHY I’VE TEAMED WITH A VERY SPECIAL NON-PROFIT CALLED BRAVE
FOR GOOD TO MAKE THIS YEAR’S “SEE YOU AT THE LIBRARY DAY” A
BIGGER SUCCESS THAN EVER.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

BRAVE FOR GOOD was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian
publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots
were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with
a tax-deductible gift.

YOUR SPONSORSHIP GIFT HELPS SEND A ‘STORY HOUR KIT’ TO EVERY
PARENT, GRANDPARENT, AND PATRIOT WHO’S ORGANIZING A “SEE YOU AT
THE LIBRARY” EVENT.

The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative
values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their
library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for
little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards,
and other specialty items.

YOUR SPONSORSHIP GIFT IS THE ONLY WAY WE CAN FUND OUR “STORY
HOURS” FOR 250,000 CHILDREN TO COUNTER THE RADICAL LEFTISTS WHO’VE
TAKEN CONTROL OF OUR LIBRARIES.

We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded
ALA.

KNOWING THAT, PLEASE CONSIDER A SPONSORSHIP GIFT OF $125. THAT’S
ENOUGH TO SPONSOR ONE ENTIRE ‘STORY HOUR KIT’ YOURSELF.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome,
Godly, and patriotic message.

WHATEVER YOU CAN GIVE WHETHER IT’S $35, $125, OR ANYTHING HIGHER OR
LOWER PLEASE SEND IN YOUR SPONSORSHIP GIFT IN THE NEXT 48 HOURS SO WE
KNOW HOW MANY LIBRARIES WE HAVE SPONSORED FOR THIS YEAR’S “SEE YOU
AT THE LIBRARY DAY.”
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,

KIRK CAMERON

AND AS A RESULT, A NEW GENERATION OF PINK-HAIRED, ACTIVIST LIBRARIANS HAVE MADE IT THEIR MISSION TO FILL LIBRARY SHELVES WITH ANTI-AMERICAN, LGBTQ-FRIENDLY, AND EXPLICITLY SEXUAL CONTENT. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. BUT HERE’S WHAT’S REALLY ALARMING. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now.
